_note: Authored 2026-09-19 with the daytime tree. Answers trace to site.json configurations and the included list, the jazz duo's setlist and repertoire.json's decades, the unamplified line on the ceremony page, and the first-learned-song line on the solo guitarist page. The music therapy answer is a plain no: a board-certified music therapist is a different, clinical booking, and nothing clinical is claimed for a performance. Questions are worded the way activity directors search.

service.name: Live music for senior living and memory care
service.serviceType: Live music entertainment for assisted living, memory care and independent living communities and senior centers
service.description: A jazz duo, upright bass and guitar, or a solo musician for the afternoon program at assisted living, memory care and independent living communities and senior centers across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor: the standards and the Great American Songbook at 65 to 72 dBA, no stage, for one date or a standing weekday afternoon, with a certificate of insurance, a W-9 and one itemised invoice in the quote.

faqs.q: Do you play at assisted living and memory care communities?
faqs.a: Yes. A solo musician or a duo plays the common area, the dining hall or the activity space of an assisted living, memory care or independent living community, and senior centers too, usually on a weekday afternoon and often as a standing monthly date. The duo is upright bass and guitar playing the standards; the solo is one guitarist, one pianist, or one singer with a guitar.

faqs.q: What music do you play for seniors?
faqs.a: The standards and the Great American Songbook, and the songs of the sixties and seventies: the Beatles, Motown, the folk songs and the country songs. Instrumentally on upright bass and guitar, or sung with a guitar when the program wants the words. Requests are taken as they come, and the first learned song a community asks for is included in every booking.

No. It's a live performance for the residents, and a board-certified music therapist is a different booking with a clinical purpose. What we bring is musicians playing the songs the residents know, at a volume that's easy to hear and easy to talk across, in the common area with no stage.

faqs.q: Can we book a standing monthly date?
faqs.a: Yes. A standing date, the same weekday afternoon each month or every other week, runs on one contract with one personal contact for the whole run, and the set changes from visit to visit. Tell us the afternoon and how often, and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price for that run of dates.

faqs.q: Do you provide a certificate of insurance and a W-9?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate of insurance naming the community as additional insured, a W-9 and one itemised invoice come in the same email as the contract, so the business office has what it needs to set up the vendor before the first visit.

faqs.q: How much does live music cost for a senior living community?
faqs.a: We publish no prices of our own. What live music costs in this market, with the source for each figure, is on the pricing page, and a weekday afternoon is priced as its own date. Send the afternoon you have in mind and how often, and we'll price it.
